risk_signals.statement: The FY2024 asset-quality shock (classified investments 13,797.16m->59,686.20m, described in the recognition-without-provisioning risk_signal below) was completely invisible in this bank's own interim Q1-Q3 2024 filings, now added to this dataset. Provision charge ran at a steady, unremarkable discrete-quarter pace through the first nine months (Q1 301.11m, Q2 371.11m, Q3 361.64m -- averaging 344.62m/quarter) while operating profit before provision kept ACCELERATING every quarter (discrete Q1 650.95m, Q2 818.82m, Q3 878.49m) and cumulative PAT grew steadily and unremarkably (110.85m -> 267.91m -> 460.91m through Q3, i.e. nothing resembling a warning sign). The entire shock hit in Q4 alone: full-year provision charge of 2,053.80m (FY2024 annual report, this dataset's own 2024_Q4.json) implies a discrete Q4 provision charge of 1,019.94m -- 2.96x the Q1-Q3 quarterly average, and by itself almost exactly equal to the entire first nine months combined (1,033.86m). Q4 alone also delivered the year's strongest discrete operating profit before provision (1,683.64m, exceeding any single prior quarter), which is what allowed full-year PAT to still rise to 812.58m (discrete Q4 PAT 351.67m, also the year's highest single quarter) despite absorbing the provisioning surge. Conclusion: an analyst relying only on this bank's own Q1-Q3 2024 interim filings would have seen accelerating, unremarkable profitability quarter over quarter, with zero visible warning of the classified-investment quadrupling disclosed only in the year-end audited accounts -- the FY2024 recognition event was a genuine year-end cliff-edge, not a gradually-emerging trend.

Classified investments (NPIs) jumped 4.33x in one year, from 13,797.16m (FY2023) to 59,686.20m (FY2024), taking the NPL ratio from 7.27% to 29.96% (both self-calculated as classified_loans/gross_loans; the bank's own reported figures are 7.12%/38.91%-coverage for FY2023 and 29.31% NPL for FY2024, consistent with the same picture). Provision for Classified Investments rose only from 5,368m to 7,829m over the same period - far short of the increase in exposure - so Gross NPI coverage collapsed from 38.91% to 13.12% (both figures reproduce exactly against the bank's own reported 'Gross NPI Coverage' ratios for these two years). The resulting unprovided classified-investment balance (59,686.20m - 7,829m = 51,857.20m) is 2.80x the bank's entire FY2024 Solo shareholders' equity (18,535.90m) - i.e. a full write-down of the unprovided exposure would wipe out equity nearly three times over. General Provision for Unclassified Investments has been nil since FY2021 (four consecutive years, FY2021-FY2024), removing what would ordinarily be a buffer against exactly this kind of shock.

Despite the FY2024 asset-quality collapse, reported Solo CRAR barely moved (14.01% at FY2023 to 14.12% at FY2024, both comfortably above the 12.5%-with-buffer requirement) - but the FY2024 annual report's own Directors' Report discloses this is only because 'Bangladesh Bank allowed us deferral... for finalizing the audited accounts without adjusting shortfall provisions where classified investments and its corresponding claims... has not been considered', under which CRAR would otherwise be stated as 15.65% (Solo); the bank's own formal Pillar-3 disclosure states the shortfall-inclusive figure of 14.12% used here. Combined with the nil general-provisioning noted above and the 13.12% coverage ratio, the stable headline CRAR is a case of capital-ratio stability driven by deferred recognition rather than genuine loss-absorption capacity - the same recognition-vs-deferral pattern flagged for ISLAMIBANK and NBL in the sector-wide FY2024 analysis (_HANDOFF.md).

NPL ratio more than doubled in a single year, from 3.64% (FY2016) to 8.29% (FY2017, self-calculated; the bank's own contemporaneous-vintage table reported 8.44%), as classified loans rose from 3,799m to 10,451m. The bank then ground this down over four years to 4.87% by FY2020 (a figure independently confirmed verbatim in that year's own Directors' Report: 'to retain the non-performing loan within 4.87% i.e. Tk. 7,764.22') before asset quality began deteriorating again from FY2021 (6.19%) through FY2022 (7.94%) and FY2023 (7.27%) on the way to the FY2024 shock described above - i.e. FY2024 was the culmination of a renewed deterioration already visible for three years, not a single-year surprise.

Solo ROE fell almost every year from 19.59% (FY2011) to a series-low 4.00% (FY2021) even as the bank nearly tripled in size (Total Assets 74,704.36m to 223,348.48m over the same span) - ROA fell in parallel from 1.82% to 0.31%. ROE partially recovered to 7.39% by FY2023 (PAT 1,360.72m, a series-high in absolute terms) before relapsing to 4.38% in FY2024 (PAT falling to 812.58m) as the asset-quality shock described above took hold. Note the bank's own Directors'-Report-narrated ROE/ROA figures (e.g. 'Return on equity was 4.59% in 2021') are calculated on a Consolidated basis and will not match the Solo figures used here (Solo ROE 4.00% for FY2021) - this is an expected, documented difference in basis, not a data error (see sources.json).

Total assets grew every year of the 14-year series except FY2020, from 74,704.36m (FY2011) to 267,928.79m (FY2024), a 3.59x increase overall, with a single small contraction from 220,478.42m (FY2019) to 217,685.39m (FY2020, -1.27%) coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic year - driven mainly by the Investments-in-Shares-and-Securities book shrinking from 32,688.66m to 9,609.75m. Growth resumed the very next year and was never interrupted again, including through the FY2017 NPL spike and the FY2024 asset-quality shock.

insights.historical_context: Standard Bank (renamed Standard Islami Bank PLC effective 10 February 2026) shows a 14-year public history in three phases. FY2011-FY2016: strong early profitability (ROE 19.59% falling steadily to 8.33%) on a rapidly growing but historically clean balance sheet (NPL ratio 2.19%-3.64%). FY2017-FY2020: a sharp NPL spike (3.64% to 8.29%) driven by a jump in classified loans from 3,799m to 10,451m, worked down over four years to 4.87% by FY2020 through disciplined recovery (verbatim-confirmed in that year's own Directors' Report) even as profitability kept compressing (ROE bottoming at 6.21% in FY2020) - a period that also includes the bank's shareholder-approved conversion from conventional to full-fledged Islamic banking (EGM 30 July 2020; Bangladesh Bank permission letter 24 Feb 2020), with the FY2021 annual report the first to drop conventional-banking terminology entirely. FY2021-FY2024: asset quality deteriorated again almost every year (NPL 6.19% to 7.94% to 7.27%) while general provisioning against unclassified investments dropped to nil for four consecutive years, culminating in FY2024's severe shock - classified investments quadrupling to 59,686.20m (29.96% of gross investments) with coverage collapsing to 13.12% and unprovided exposure reaching 2.80x total equity, while reported CRAR stayed flat only because of a Bangladesh-Bank-granted provisioning deferral disclosed in the bank's own report. Total assets grew in every year of the series except FY2020 (a small, COVID-19-linked -1.27% contraction, 220,478.42m to 217,685.39m), resuming growth the following year regardless of the credit cycle.

sources.notes: annual_reports/STANDBANKL contains 13 PDFs already text-extracted (pdftotext -layout) prior to this research: 2011-2012 and 2014-2024 (FY2013 missing from the archive). Achieved Q4/year-end coverage for all 14 of those years plus a recovered FY2013, using each year's own report wherever legible plus four adjacent-report comparative columns to cover FY2012, FY2013, FY2015 and one EPS gap in FY2018. REPORTING BASIS: Solo (standalone, not consolidated), confirmed for every year 2011-2024. The bank has presented a 'Consolidated Balance Sheet'/'Consolidated Profit and Loss Account' (for itself plus small subsidiaries - Standard Exchange Co. (UK) Ltd., Standard Co. (USA) Inc., SBL Capital Management Ltd., SBL Securities Ltd.) alongside its own Solo statements in every report since at least FY2011; from FY2023 onward the Solo statements are explicitly labelled 'Balance Sheet-Solo Basis' / 'Profit and Loss Account-Solo Basis' on their face, confirming the basis directly. For FY2011-2022 the Solo statement was identified by (a) its heading naming only 'Standard Bank Limited' / 'Standard Bank PLC.' without 'and Subsidiaries' or 'Consolidated', (b) cross-checking its Total Assets against the following year's report's own comparative column for the same date, and (c) for capital adequacy specifically, the formal Basel-III Pillar-3 'Quantitative Disclosure' table's explicit 'For stand alone:' sub-section (present in every report from FY2011 onward) which gives a directly-labelled Solo Capital-to-Risk-Weighted-Asset Ratio (CRAR) independent of the Balance Sheet basis question. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THE BANK'S OWN 'FIVE YEAR(S) FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS' TABLES: every edition of this table found (in the FY2016, FY2019, FY2021, FY2023 and FY2024 reports) reproduces figures that are consistently 0.3%-11% ABOVE the confirmed Solo Balance Sheet/P&L for the same year (verified repeatedly: e.g. FY2018 Total Assets 197,148m in the table vs 195,764.45m in the confirmed Solo Balance Sheet; FY2016 PAT 1,088m in the table vs 1,043.56m in the confirmed Solo P&L) - i.e. this table is Consolidated-basis throughout, not Solo, DESPITE not being labelled as such. It is therefore NOT used in this dataset for any Balance Sheet or Profit-and-Loss aggregate (Total Assets, Deposits, Loans, Equity, Interest Income, PAT, EPS, ROE, ROA, NAV/share) - those are always taken from the actual Solo financial statements or a Solo comparative column instead. The table IS used, with cross-validation, for: (i) classified-loan/NPL amounts (confirmed Solo-equivalent - a bank's book of 'loans and advances' or Bangladesh-Bank-regulated 'investments' is inherently a Solo/bank-only concept that a brokerage or exchange-house subsidiary does not contribute to; the FY2019 report's classified-loan note 7.9 figure of 9,232,447,399 for FY2019 reproduces exactly in that report's own highlights table and in the FY2020 report's comparative), (ii) branch/employee/shareholder counts, and (iii) market price per share (a traded-security fact, not an accounting policy choice, so it cannot differ by consolidation basis). NPL RATIO METHODOLOGY: because the bank's own highlights tables disagree with each other across vintages for the SAME historical year (e.g. FY2017's NPL ratio is shown as 8.44% in the FY2019 report's table but 7.42% in the FY2021 report's table for the identical year, with the identical classified-loan amount of 10,451m in both - implying the LOANS denominator itself was redefined/enlarged in the later vintage, most plausibly by folding in a Consolidated, margin-loan-inclusive loan book), this dataset computes npl_pct itself for every year as classified_loans / gross_loans, both taken from confirmed-Solo sources, rather than trusting any single vintage of the reported ratio. This self-computed ratio was independently corroborated to within a few hundredths of a percentage point against contemporaneous Directors' Report prose in three separate years (FY2011 2.19%, FY2020 4.87% verbatim 'Tk. 7,764.22', FY2023 7.27% verbatim) and against the bank's own 'Gross NPI Coverage' cross-ratio (provision_classified/classified_loans) for FY2024 (13.12% both ways) - giving confidence in the method even where a given year's own highlights-table NPL% does not reconcile. GENERALLY: the bank's own Directors'-Report-prose ROE/ROA/NPL narrative mentions are, on inspection, calculated on the same Consolidated basis as the highlights table (e.g. FY2021's narrated 'Return on equity was 4.59%' reproduces exactly from Consolidated PAT 791.73m / Consolidated equity 17,253.21m, not this dataset's Solo PAT 686.35m / Solo equity 17,175.44m used for the 4.00% ROE reported here) - this is expected and is not treated as an error each year, only flagged here once. TERMINOLOGY: the bank operated a small 'Islami Banking Window' alongside conventional banking from 2009, so FY2011-2020 statements already carry dual labels ('Loans, Cash Credits, Overdraft etc./ Investments', 'Interest Income / Profit on Investment'). Shareholders approved converting the whole bank to full-fledged Islamic banking at a 28th EGM on 30 July 2020 (Bangladesh Bank permission letter BRPD(P-3)/745(43)/2020-2221 dated 24 Feb 2020); the FY2021 annual report is the first to drop conventional terminology entirely (Balance Sheet's main financing line becomes pure 'INVESTMENTS'; the credit-quality schedule is retitled 'Statement of Non-Performing Investment', from 'Statement of Non-Performing Loan' through FY2020). This dataset normalises metric names to the conventional-banking vocabulary (gross_loans, interest_income, npl_pct, etc.) across the whole 2011-2024 span for cross-bank and cross-year comparability, while original_metric_name in each year's line_items preserves the bank's own contemporaneous label, so the exact wording shift is fully traceable. On 10 February 2026, Bangladesh Bank announced the bank's rename from 'Standard Bank PLC' to 'Standard Islami Bank PLC' following its full conversion to a Shariah-compliant institution; this is purely a corporate-name change (the DSE ticker STANDBANKL is unchanged) and does not itself mark any additional accounting-basis shift beyond the FY2021 terminology change already described.

Per project standing rule, a full quarterly entry is not fabricated from these headline figures alone - FY2025 is recorded as a genuine 'not yet available' gap, not a permanent one, since the underlying audited financial statements plainly exist and were approved less than a month before this research. Cash Dividend history on dsebd.org ('2.50% 2023, 2.50% 2022, 3% 2021, 2.5% 2020, 5% 2019, 5% 2016, 10% 2013') notably omits any FY2024 or FY2025 entry, suggesting no cash dividend was declared for either year - consistent with the FY2024 asset-quality shock.

OVERVIEW (see per-quarter entries below for individual sourcing/basis detail). Found the bank's dedicated interim-filings page at https://www.standardbankbd.com/en/page/dynamic-list/quarterly-half-yearly-reports -- a CMS-rendered listing distinct from the Annual Reports page, containing 39 directly-downloadable PDF links (file?id=<uuid>.pdf) spanning 2010-2026 (confirmed complete/non-paginated by parsing the raw HTML table directly, not just an AI summary of it). The bank's OLD static file structure (standardbankbd.com/Content/Files/Financials/...) is now fully DEAD on the live site -- every path under that prefix, real or guessed, returns an identical ~117KB HTML single-page-app shell at HTTP 200 (a serious trap: 'file' and a plain HTTP-status check both suggest success; only inspecting the actual bytes reveals it is not a PDF). Filled the gaps this left (specific quarters whose exact filename the CMS listing didn't carry) using the Wayback Machine's CDX API against that same dead path prefix, which still holds captures of it from when it was live -- this recovered Q1 2023, Q3 2023, Q2/Q3 2024, and Q2/Q3 2025 (with the last two ultimately proving unrecoverable in full, see their own notes below) plus several older gaps (Q3 2019, Q3 2020, Q1/Q3 2021, H1 2022). TWO INDEPENDENT INSTANCES of Wayback's known 'truncated at a round power-of-2 byte boundary' artifact were hit and worked around this session, beyond the previously-documented 1,048,576-byte (1 MiB) case: a second, larger 5,242,880-byte (5 MiB) truncation tier affecting some 2024-2025-era captures specifically (2024 Q3 recovered via a different, complete-digest capture; 2025 Q2 and Q3 could NOT be recovered this way since every available capture of each shares the identical truncated digest -- confirmed via qpdf/mutool/PyMuPDF repair attempts, all of which fail because the truncation cuts through a structural object (the page tree / xref stream), not just trailing content). BASIS DISCOVERY (materially changes the picture from the prior session's placeholder note): this bank's interim filings are NOT Consolidated-only across the board. FY2011 through FY2015-Q1 filings are genuinely Consolidated-only (no Solo section exists in the condensed single-page or short multi-page templates used in that era, confirmed by reading every page of each). Starting with the half-year ended 30 June 2015, every quarterly/half-yearly filing (with one single-quarter exception, FY2023-Q1) contains a genuine second 'Balance Sheet'/'Profit and Loss Account' section -- headed identically to the Consolidated one but WITHOUT the word 'Consolidated', easy to miss on a first pass -- that is Solo, matching the main annual Q4 series' basis. Confirmed genuinely Solo, not a mislabeled repeat: (a) its own figures are consistently smaller than the Consolidated section earlier in the same document, and (b) in every single case checked (14 years' worth), its own prior-year-end comparator column reproduces this dataset's own independently-sourced annual Q4 Solo total_assets figure exactly or to within immaterial rounding -- a strong, repeated cross-validation. From FY2021 onward the bank's own filings explicitly label these sections 'Balance Sheet-Solo Basis'/'Profit and Loss Account-Solo Basis' on their face, removing any ambiguity. EXTRACTION METHOD: pdftotext -layout where the PDF's embedded text layer was usable (most 2021-2025 filings, plus several 2012-2013 ones); OCR (pdftoppm at 300dpi + tesseract --psm 6) for scanned/image-only PDFs (common in 2011-2020) and for the small number of text-layer PDFs whose complex multi-column layout defeated pdftotext's column reconstruction specifically for the P&L table (2011 Q1/Q2, 2013 Q2/Q3) -- OCR consistently outperformed pdftotext on this bank's dense tables even where a text layer existed. Every quarter's key totals were cross-checked against (i) the balance-sheet identity, (ii) PBT-tax=PAT, (iii) the operating-income-equals-sum-of-components identity, and (iv) wherever possible, the same figure's reappearance as a comparator column in an adjacent quarter's own filing or as this dataset's own independently-sourced annual Q4 figure -- all done programmatically against the final written JSON files, not just by eye. Two quarters found and downloaded (2011 Q3, 2014 Q1) were deliberately NOT written up despite a genuine source PDF existing, because OCR quality on those two specific condensed-page scans (tried at 200/300/400dpi) was too unreliable to transcribe with confidence -- per project policy, never fabricate; see their own notes below and the archived OCR text (clearly marked OCR-UNRELIABLE-not-used) kept in annual_reports/STANDBANKL/ for a future session's retry. All downloaded PDFs deleted after extraction; extracted text archived to annual_reports/STANDBANKL/standbankl-quarterly-<year>-<q>.txt for every quarter actually used.
